The files in this folder are data of the Federal Office of Meteorology and
Climatology MeteoSwiss, measured by the automatic weather stations of its
network SwissMetNet and published as Open Data under Creative Commons
CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/, by MeteoSwiss's
terms of use, https://opendatadocs.meteoswiss.ch/general/terms-of-use.
Source: MeteoSwiss. The credit is no statement that MeteoSwiss supports
this project or its use of the data. They are not covered by the licence
of the code around them.

They were recorded on 2026-11-22 from https://data.geo.admin.ch/, without
a key, with curl, single GET requests.

VQHA80.csv and ogd-smn_meta_stations.csv are the whole answers to the
adapter's two requests, unchanged, both asked at 08:09:13 UTC:

    VQHA80.csv                 GET /ch.meteoschweiz.messwerte-aktuell/VQHA80.csv
                               16,210 bytes: 159 rows, the current values of
                               every station; Last-Modified 08:00:10 UTC,
                               values of 07:50 UTC
    ogd-smn_meta_stations.csv  GET /ch.meteoschweiz.ogd-smn/ogd-smn_meta_stations.csv
                               151,779 bytes: 158 stations; Last-Modified
                               04:19:30 UTC; ISO 8859-1, lines end in CR LF

VQHA80.csv has a row for MRP, which the station list does not hold, with
no value in it.

ogd-smn_meta_parameters.csv is MeteoSwiss's description of its parameters,
GET /ch.meteoschweiz.ogd-smn/ogd-smn_meta_parameters.csv, asked right after
the two (50,180 bytes), cut down to its header and the six rows of the
parameters the adapter reads, each byte for byte as MeteoSwiss wrote it
(ISO 8859-1, CR LF). A test holds the adapter's units against it.

The folder evening/ holds three station files of ten-minute values, asked
at 08:11:22 and 08:11:23 UTC:

    evening/ogd-smn_STATION_t_recent.csv
        GET /ch.meteoschweiz.ogd-smn/STATION/ogd-smn_STATION_t_recent.csv

for the stations dav (Davos), sam (Samedan) and wfj (Weissfluhjoch). Each
answer was the station's values of 2026 up to the day before, 5.6 to 6.5
MB; kept here is its header line and its twelve rows from 18:00 to 19:50
UTC on 2026-11-18, byte for byte. The adapter does not ask for these
files. They are here for the next two files.

stations_evening.csv and VQHA80_evening.csv are NOT answers of MeteoSwiss
as it gave them. They are a sample for the server's development mode, whose
clock stands at 19:05 UTC on 2026-11-18, four days before this source was
recorded; the file of current values holds the newest values only.

    stations_evening.csv   ogd-smn_meta_stations.csv cut down to its
                           header and the rows of DAV, SAM and WFJ, byte
                           for byte
    VQHA80_evening.csv     the header of VQHA80.csv and a row for each of
                           the three stations at 202611181850, with each
                           column's value from that station's row of
                           18.11.2026 18:50 in evening/, written with two
                           decimals as VQHA80.csv writes them, and "-"
                           where the station's file has no value or no
                           such column (the columns of the towers)

So every value in the sample is one MeteoSwiss gave, for the station, the
parameter and the moment the sample says: 18:50 UTC on 2026-11-18, fifteen
minutes before the development mode's clock. A test of this crate holds
every value of the sample against the station's file.

stations_damaged.csv and VQHA80_damaged.csv are not MeteoSwiss's data: they
are the two evening files with things changed by hand, to test how the
adapter reports what it cannot read. The test that uses them says what was
changed.

To record them again: fetch the two files of a run in one go and replace
them; set the moment in tests/pipeline.rs; run the tests with
VENTI_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 and review what changed. The counts the tests pin
(stations, stations with a wind, the 24 east of 9.4° E) are of that moment
and may differ.

A value in these files is what an instrument reported. It is no statement
that a place can be flown.
